reason: The phospholipids appear to form the cell surface, but I don't yet know how the game builds it.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to start building or testing the surface.

alternatives.reason: Oxygen is supposed to cross the surface, but the membrane may need to be assembled first.

effect: Water and phospholipids formed membrane patches, so I can now test what crosses them.
reaction: The two layers with their heads facing water make the surface easier to picture.
reason: The goal says oxygen should enter, and its picture shows uncharged molecules without a carrier.
expectation: Oxygen will cross the lipid-only membrane into the cell.

effect: Oxygen can cross the lipid region directly, moving inward from where it is more concentrated.
reaction: The picture makes oxygen's path into the cell clear.
reason: The other part of the first goal is water exchange, so I'll test water against the lipid-only patches before adding a channel.
expectation: Water will exchange across the lipid-only membrane, though I don't know how readily.

alternatives.reason: The channel could provide a water route, but testing the lipid-only patch first may show what changes.

effect: Water crosses the lipid-only patch slowly in both directions, with net movement toward the side with more solutes that cannot cross.
reaction: Comparing the two directions makes water exchange clearer.
reason: The aquaporin picture shows a water pore, so adding it should let me compare the channel route with the lipid-only route.
expectation: The channel will provide a route for water and allow a comparison with slow exchange through lipid.

effect: The aquaporin speeds water exchange while net movement still favors the side with more non-crossing solutes; the oxygen and water goal is complete.
reaction: The side-by-side comparison makes the channel's effect clear.
reason: The remaining goal calls for a passive sodium route, and the open sodium channel is pictured as a pore through the membrane.
expectation: The channel will provide a route for sodium to enter, though the sodium solution may also need to be used.

alternatives.reason: I could test sodium against the lipid-only patch first, but the goal specifically calls for a route.

effect: The open channel let sodium enter without spending ATP under the shown conditions, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was useful to see that the channel provides a route rather than pushing sodium in.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing water through lipid and then adding aquaporin was most worthwhile: the comparison showed that water crosses both ways but moves faster through the channel.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial membrane assembly was less engaging because inspection revealed only one partner and completed it automatically, though the resulting picture helped explain the layers.

surprise.text: I was surprised that water could cross the lipid-only patch at all, even though it did so slowly.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely arbitrary. I did not initially know how to build the membrane, so I relied on the compatibility hint for the first pairing.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: comparing the water routes made the structures' different jobs understandable, and I would be curious to see what comes next.
